divergence.note: conservative gap = a pair no row names (exported UNKNOWN vs implicit R0); eligibility finding = same kind, different eligibility reading (`valid`/`loss_mask`); conflict = different kind for the same pair, or a different mate set.  Only a conflict fails the run.

eligibility_finding.decision: applied on Lead ruling: the divergence was an eligibility defect, not a contract detail.  Withdrawn rows are no longer supplied by any reader; the measured cost is in data/a12_reports/negfix_eligibility.json
eligibility_finding.frozen_gate: eligible_as_negative == (kind in {R0,R1} and valid and loss_mask)
eligibility_finding.mechanism: FIXED (docs/a12/relation_negatives.md §9.1.2): eligibility now has one truth source (relations.legal_negative.resolve_negative_eligibility) and every reader consumes it.  Before the fix, training.sampler.PoolIndex.confirmed() recomputed confirmation from relation() alone (rel in {R0,R1,R2}) and relations.gallery.RelationsIndex.confirmed() accepted an explicit edge regardless of its valid flag, so the live pool and the sampler's adapter offered rows the exported reader refused.
eligibility_finding.one_line_fix: applied: every reader answers negative_eligibility(a, b) from the row's own valid/loss_mask flags (relations/legal_negative.py), and PoolIndex/RelationsIndex.confirmed() consume it instead of recomputing from the kind
